verdict.reasoning: Patient describes “diarrhea… super watery” and says “it’s been about three days now.”
Patient reports going “almost every hour I’m awake” with “super watery” stools and, when asked, states “No… there’s nothing like that” regarding blood in stools.

Patient locates the cramp “like at the bottom… pretty like in the middle” but rates it as “maybe… a six or seven” while also saying “I can pretend that I don’t feel it… people don’t really notice,” implying more moderate pain. The transcript does not clearly support a 6–7/10 severity and portrays it as mild-to-moderate, making the specific high rating inconsistent with the described impact.
Patient says “I definitely feel kind of nauseous” when asked about nausea/vomiting.
Patient reports vomiting and links it to milk: “whenever I have like milk… I just feel like I want to vomit… one time I… had some milk and I just completely vomited it.”
Patient says “I feel kind of really hot all the time… I haven’t actually done any temperature reading,” indicating feeling febrile without measuring temperature.
Patient states fluids “go down, but it just feels like it’s going straight through” and reports urinating “less frequently maybe, but it seems to be okay.”
Patient says “my brother has had… something like this… for five days” and that he “is getting better, but I’m not really sure,” matching similar illness for 5 days and improving.
When asked about medical history, patient replies “Yeah, I think otherwise I’m fit… I can’t think of any related medical history… no, I don’t think so,” indicating no past medical history reported.
Patient says “I’ve been taking some, like, paracetamols and stuff like that lately, but… I’m not on any regular medication,” consistent with PRN use.
To allergy question, patient answers “I don’t have any allergies that I know of,” i.e., NKDA.
Patient reports “My dad actually has colon cancer… he’s sort of in his third stage,” matching stage III colon cancer.
Patient says “I live with my sister and my mum,” matching living with mother and sister.
Patient states “I work at an office in central London… I work in government,” consistent with a government office job.
Patient reports “I smoke… socially but not like regularly… if it’s a Friday… I might have a cigarette,” consistent with social smoking.
Patient says “I might have a beer during the weekdays… maybe on Fridays I have more alcohol… once or twice a month… we’ll drink a lot,” matching weekday beer and monthly binge drinking.

Doctor concludes: “your symptoms are suggestive of something called gastroenteritis… a basic infection of your tummy… Make sure you drink plenty of fluids,” and notes frequent watery diarrhea, implying acute gastroenteritis with dehydration risk.
Doctor ties symptoms together: “I think your symptoms are suggestive of… gastroenteritis,” after discussing abdominal pain and nausea/vomiting, implying these are due to the gastroenteritis.
Doctor says “I’ll make a note of that because it’s always important to know these kind of details” about the father’s colon cancer, but does not explicitly state it is flagged for future screening.

Doctor advises “you can get things like diurelite, which is a fluid replacement… from the pharmacy” and later “clear fluids… soft diet, things like soup, mash, and then gradually build up,” matching oral rehydration and progression to soft diet.
Doctor says “You can try… regular paracetamol if you are feeling feverish” and confirms “If you’ve got bit of tummy pain, if you’re feeling feverish, then I think paracetamol is very sensible.”
Doctor advises “Try and avoid alcohol if you can” but does not advise avoiding dairy; dairy is only discussed as a trigger for vomiting by the patient, not as formal advice to avoid it.
No instruction is given to “monitor hydration by tracking urine output and dizziness”; only general concern about dehydration is expressed and that urine is “okay.”

Doctor says “if your symptoms aren’t settling down in the next couple of days, so 48 hours, I want you to give me a call back… if you are getting dehydrated, then we need to do further investigations,” which aligns with safety-net advice for lack of improvement and dehydration risk, though vomiting is not specifically mentioned.
The transcript mentions “we need to do further investigations” if dehydrated but does not specify stool cultures, blood tests, or in-person examination.
